newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt recovers composure by the close after MPS.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt recovers composure by the close after MPS.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.95 PCT (PREV 8.05) US 5-YR 6.11 (PREV 6.06)
* NZ debt mkts sell on RBNZ statement but recover by close
* High NZ dollar buoys debt markets but profit-taking sees yields end a touch higher
* Scope seen for short rates to move lower
New Zealand debt markets had recovered their composure by the close on Tuesday after a brief panic when the Reserve Bank released a bearish statement early in the session.

Speaking at the presentation of the bank's six-monthly monetary policy statement (MPS), Governor Don Brash said the new 0-3 percent target band for core inflation meant conditions could be looser than otherwise might have been the case.

He endorsed the easing that has already taken place since the October 12 election, but said the market's exuberant reaction to the formation of a centre-right National-New Zealand First coalition government last week was "somewhat excessive".
"The market sold off initially on that word Brash used "excessive" -- that gave the market a bit of a fright," said one dealer.

He said the 90-day bank bill rate spiked about 15 points on the comments but quickly came back on a stronger New Zealand currency "and just when people started to look at what had been said a little bit closer".
Rates moved below their Monday night closes by a few points before profit-taking saw them close a touch higher.
"The short bonds have been given on a little bit on offshore profit-taking, but all in all it all bodes reasonably well, particularly with the Kiwi as strong as it is," the dealer said.
The New Zealand dollar climbed strongly after the MPS was released, closing at US$0.7069/76 and at 67.41 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6985/92 and 66.65 at the open.

The MPS forecasts assumed 90-day bank bills at 9.0 percent, but the bank said events since the MPS was finalised meant 90-days at 8.50 percent and the TWI at 66.5 might be more consistent with overall conditions.
Brash also said the bank could "accept monetary conditions which are either a little firmer than those represented by that level, or a little easier as over the last few days".
"Although Brash talked about 66.5 (TWI) and 8.5 (90-day rate), he also said that he could accommodate easier or tigher conditions," a dealer said.
"A lot of people have talked about 7.65 or 7.5 percent (for the 90-day rate), so I wouldn't be at all surprised if we do have a look towards there in the not-too-distant future."
-- Matthew Brockett (64 4) 473-3736
